$comment: GENERATED FILE, DO NOT EDIT. Source: shared/protocol/openapi.yaml. Regenerate with `pnpm protocol:generate`.

UuidV7.description: Canonical lowercase UUID version 7 (time ordered), generated by the agent.

AgentVersion.description: Semantic version of the agent binary.

HeartbeatIntervalSeconds.description: Interval, in seconds, between two heartbeats.

EnrollmentToken.description:
Single-use enrollment token created in the console (valid 24 h): `dbe_` + 43 base64url chars
(256 random bits). Stored hashed by the console.

AgentSecret.description:
Agent secret: `dbs_` + 43 base64url chars (256 random bits from a CSPRNG). Issued by the console
in the `/enroll` response, generated by the agent for `/rotate`. Sent only in the
`Authorization` header afterwards. Never logged by either side. The console rejects obviously
low-entropy values (e.g. fewer than 16 distinct characters in the 43-character body, such as a
single repeated character) with `400` `invalid_secret`.

Hostname.description: Host name of the agent host (RFC 1123), informational.

TargetId.description:
Identifier of a target, as declared in `agent.yaml` (ADR-0006). Unique per agent. A slug: it
cannot contain a host name, address or credential.

ClassifiersVersion.description: Version of the classifier set, `YYYY.MM.N`, e.g. `2026.09.1`.

Fingerprint.description:
`HMAC-SHA256(agent_local_key, normalized_value)`, lowercase hex. The key never leaves the agent,
so fingerprints only correlate values seen by the same agent.

MaskedSample.description:
Sample masked by `classifiers::masking` (e.g. `j*******@e******.com`,
`FR76 **** **** **** **** ***1 89`). Schema rules: contains at least one `*`, no run of more than
4 consecutive letters or digits, no combining mark, no control / format / private-use / line
separator character. The console additionally requires at least 50 % of the non-separator characters (letters, digits
and `*`; spaces and punctuation ignored) to be `*`: `06 ** ** ** 78` passes (6 of 10).

Identifier.description:
**Normalized** name of a database object: database, schema, table, collection, column, field
path, LDAP suffix, container or attribute. Never a value, never a record identifier.

Normalization rules (`x-databastion-normalized-name`), applied by the agent before the uplink:
- array indices in a path become `[]` (`orders.3.email` -> `orders[].email`);
- dynamic keys (map keys, keys that look like identifiers or values) and any name segment
  matched by a classifier become `*` (`contacts.jane@example.com.phone` -> `contacts.*.phone`);
- an LDAP entry DN is reduced to its parent container (`uid=jdoe,ou=people,dc=example,dc=com`
  -> `ou=people,dc=example,dc=com`); attribute types are lowercased;
- a name that still does not match this schema is replaced by `*`.

Pattern: either a plain name, which excludes `@ = : ; / \ ' "`, backquote, `< > ( ) ,` and
control / format characters (so no e-mail address, `key=value`, URL or SQL fragment), or an LDAP
container DN made only of `ou=`, `dc=`, `o=`, `c=`, `l=`, `st=` RDNs (never `uid=` / `cn=`).

not.description:
No name, and no `.`-separated path segment, made only of 9 or more digits and separators
(phone numbers, account or card numbers used as keys).

IdentifierPattern.description:
Console-provided filter on object names: an exact name, or a glob with `*` and `?`. The agent
treats it as a name filter only and never interpolates it into a query.

Count.description: Non-negative integer counter, bounded to the JavaScript safe integer range.

UnixSocketPath.description:
Absolute path of a local Unix socket under a well-known runtime directory (`/run`, `/var/run`,
`/tmp`, `/var/lib/mysql`), e.g. `/var/run/postgresql/.s.PGSQL.5432`. No segment starting with
`..`. The agent only reports sockets from its fixed probe list.

ClientAddress.description:
IPv4 or IPv6 literal of the database client as logged by the engine, or `local` for a Unix socket
connection. Never a host name.

Connector.description: Agent connector (Cargo feature). `mysql` covers MySQL and MariaDB.

ConnectorList.description: Connectors compiled in and enabled in this agent.

AuditLevel.description:
Audit level actually reached for a target (docs/08-engine-capabilities.md). Reported honestly:
e.g. PostgreSQL without pgaudit is `limited`, MySQL Community `partial`, MongoDB Community
`limited` (or `partial` with profiler level 2), a target with audit disabled `none`.

AuditSource.description: Native source used for Audit on a target.

Edition.description: Engine edition or distribution, when the agent can tell.

FailureCode.description:
Closed set of failure causes. Driver or engine messages are never sent (they can contain values
or query text); `engine_code` may carry the engine's numeric / SQLSTATE code.

EngineCode.description: Engine error code (SQLSTATE, MySQL / MongoDB numeric code, LDAP result code). No text.

Error.description:
Common error body for every non-2xx response. `message` is a fixed, generic English sentence chosen
by the console; it **never echoes submitted values**. Validation `details` point to the offending
location with a JSON pointer that the console builds **only from property names known to this
schema** and array indices: an unknown property is reported on its parent object, never by its
(possibly sensitive) name.

min_protocol.description: Present on `426`; minimum protocol major version accepted by the console.

pointer.description: JSON pointer into the submitted body (e.g. `/findings/3/confidence`); `""` for the root.

EnrollResponse.description:
The agent identity. The agent's HMAC key is generated locally after enrollment and never
appears in this protocol.

RotateRequest.description:
Body of `POST /rotate`. A new rotation is authenticated with the current secret while no secret
is pending (`S0`); a retry is authenticated with the same `S0` and resends the same
`new_secret` (`S1`), which is answered `duplicate` while `S1` is pending and, after its
promotion, at any time within the late-retry bound (see `POST /rotate`). `new_secret` is
generated by the agent and persisted as pending before the call. Unless `S0` is stale, a body
that fails validation, or a `new_secret` equal to the authenticating secret or obviously
low-entropy, is rejected with `400` (`invalid_request` / `invalid_secret`) before any duplicate
or conflict check; with a stale `S0` (recognized after the 60 s tolerance window), any request
other than a late retry is a `409` `rotation_conflict`.

job_id.description: The `agent.rotate_secret` job that requested this rotation, if any.

RotateResponse.description:
Answer to an accepted `POST /rotate`: a new pending secret, or an idempotent retry (`duplicate`).
Carries no secret.

grace_expires_at.description:
Deadline at which the pending secret is promoted and the previous one revoked, if the new
secret has not been used before. At most 3600 s after the first registration; never extended
by a retry.

duplicate.description:
`true` when the request was authenticated with `S0` and this exact secret is already pending,
or is the current secret promoted from it (idempotent or late retry). `grace_expires_at` is
then the original deadline.

MetricsMap.description:
Internal metrics as a bounded `name -> number` map (counters, gauges, durations in seconds).
The only open-keyed object of the protocol: names are restricted to `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,63}$`
and values to numbers, so it cannot carry text.

The console re-exposes them on `/metrics` under the distinct prefix `databastion_agent_reported_`
with labels `agent_id` (and `target_id` for target metrics), so an agent can never shadow a
console-computed metric such as `databastion_agent_last_seen_seconds`. Names on the console's
reserved list (e.g. `last_seen_seconds`, `up`, `revoked`) are ignored.

ts.description: Agent clock when the heartbeat was built (lets the console detect clock skew).

targets.description: Status of every target declared in `agent.yaml`.

detected_targets.description:
Engines detected on the **local host** but not configured (ADR-0006), as suggestions for the
console's configuration wizard. Never a target network address, never a process command line.

running_jobs.description: Jobs currently executing, so the console can detect lost jobs.

server_version.description:
Engine version as reported by the server (e.g. `16.4`, `11.4.3`, `7.0.12`, `2.6.8`). Omitted
when the reported string does not match this pattern.

reachable.description: Whether the last connection attempt with the configured read-only account succeeded.

last_error.description: Cause of the last failed `check()` or connection, if any.

DetectedTarget.description:
A local engine spotted by a Unix socket, a local listening port or a process name. At least one
of `unix_socket`, `port`, `process` is present. The agent never connects to a detected target.

port.description: Local listening TCP port. The listening address is not reported.

process.description: Process name only (the command line may contain secrets and is never read or sent).

oldest_age_s.description: Age, in seconds, of the oldest spooled batch.

dropped_batches.description: Batches dropped since start (spool full, or rejected with a non-retryable 4xx).

dropped_items.description: Individual findings / events dropped since start after a `400` or `404` pointing at them.

Job.description:
A console order, discriminated by `type`. Jobs never carry a secret, a credential, a connection
string or configuration content: targets and credentials live in the agent's local `agent.yaml`.

expires_at.description: The agent must not start the job after this instant (reports `failed` / `expired`).

DiscoveryScanParams.description:
Bounds of a Discovery scan (invariant I4). The agent also applies its own local hard limits and
a per-statement timeout on every query.

sample_rows.description: Maximum rows (documents, entries) sampled per object.

max_duration_s.description: Wall-clock budget of the whole scan.

statement_timeout_ms.description: Timeout applied to each query against the target.

databases.description:
Databases (or LDAP suffixes) to include. Absent = all visible to the account. An empty list is
rejected (`minItems: 1`) so that a "none selected" bug can never widen a scan to everything.

schemas.description: Schemas to include (PostgreSQL). Absent = all. An empty list is rejected (`minItems: 1`).

include_objects.description:
Tables / collections / objectClasses to include. Absent = all. An empty list is rejected
(`minItems: 1`).

exclude_objects.description:
Tables / collections / objectClasses to skip. Absent or empty = nothing skipped (an empty list
cannot widen the scan beyond the include filters, so it is accepted).

classifiers.description:
Restrict the scan to these classifiers. Absent = all classifiers of `classifiers_version`.
An empty list is rejected (`minItems: 1`): it never means "no classifiers" nor "all".

AuditConfigureParams.description:
Audit settings for one target. Replaces the previous settings as a whole. Detection thresholds
and scoring are applied by the console's worker; these settings only drive collection and
pre-aggregation on the agent.

aggregation_window_s.description: Pre-aggregation window (same principal, object set and action).

poll_interval_s.description: Polling interval for polled sources (`performance_schema`, `pg_stat_activity`, `cn=accesslog`, profiler).

min_rows.description:
Events on objects that are not listed in `sensitive_objects` and carry no signal are only
reported when they return at least this many rows.

sensitive_objects.description:
Objects classified as sensitive by Discovery, whose accesses are always reported. Absent or
empty = no object is flagged sensitive: the settings replace the previous ones as a whole, so
an empty list legitimately clears them. An empty list narrows reporting to events that carry
a signal or reach `min_rows`; it can never widen what is reported.

AgentConfigReloadJob.description:
Asks the agent to re-read its **local** `agent.yaml`. The job carries no configuration: targets and
credentials never transit through the console (invariant I3).

AgentRotateSecretJob.description:
Asks the agent to rotate its secret. **Carries no secret**: the agent generates the new secret and
registers it with `POST /rotate`. Suspected compromise is handled by revocation and
re-enrollment, not by this job. The console never issues it while a secret is pending, nor within
60 s of a promotion; the agent defers such a job received within 60 s of a promotion
(ADR-0010).

JobStatusUpdate.description: `error` is required when `status` is `failed`, and forbidden otherwise.

findings.description: Findings reported so far for this job.

batches.description:
Findings batches sent so far for this job. On `succeeded`, lets the console check that it
received all of them.

duplicate.description: `true` when this (`agent_id`, `batch_id`) had already been received with the same content; the batch was not processed again.

FindingsBatch.description: Serialized size at most 1 MiB (agent-side bound, `x-databastion-max-bytes`).

job_id.description: The `discovery.scan` job that produced these findings.

Finding.description:
A location contains a sensitive data type. `matched <= sampled` (checked by the console).
No raw value: only masked samples and HMAC fingerprints.

estimated_rows.description: Estimated size of the object (rows, documents, entries), from engine statistics.

Location.description:
Where the data lives, down to the column / field / attribute; never a record. All names are
normalized (see `Identifier`).
PostgreSQL: database, schema, table, column. MySQL / MariaDB: database, table, column (no schema).
MongoDB: database, collection, normalized field path. OpenLDAP: suffix (as `database`),
objectClass or container (as `object`, never an entry DN), attribute.

EventsBatch.description: Serialized size at most 1 MiB (agent-side bound, `x-databastion-max-bytes`).

AccessEvent.description:
Normalized access event, pre-aggregated by the agent. Contains no query text, no bound parameter
and no returned value: only who, what object, which action, how many rows, and signals.
`read` and `write` events name at least one object.

action.description: `auth_failure`: failed authentication (the account name is then usually fingerprinted).

rows.description: Rows (documents, entries) returned or affected, when the source provides it.

aggregated_count.description: Number of raw events merged into this one.

Principal.description:
Who accessed. Exactly one of `db_user` / `db_user_fingerprint`. For a failed authentication with
an account that does not exist on the target (the attempted name may be a mistyped password), and
for any account name that does not match the `db_user` pattern, the agent sends
`db_user_fingerprint` instead of the name. The console escapes `db_user` and `application` on
display.

db_user.description: Database account (or LDAP bind DN) as logged by the engine.

application.description:
Client-declared application name (`application_name`, `appName`). The agent replaces every
character outside `[A-Za-z0-9 ._:/+-]` with `_` and truncates to 64 characters.

ObjectRef.description: Object reached by an access. Names are normalized (see `Identifier`); never an LDAP entry DN.
